gloss: to gaze at, to stare at

definitions.gloss: to gaze at, to stare at
definitions.explanation: To look at someone or something intently and continuously, often with emotional intensity or deep attention.
To look at something carefully in order to understand it better (figurative use).

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{彼|かれ}の{目|め}を{見|み}つめた。
{子供|こども}が{不思議|ふしぎ}そうに{私|わたし}を{見|み}つめていた。
examples.english: The child was staring at me with a curious look.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{人生|じんせい}を{見|み}つめ{直|なお}す{時間|じかん}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: I need time to take a hard look at my life.
examples.notes: [Note: {見|み}つめ{直|なお}す means to reexamine or reconsider]

notes:
{見|み}つめる is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) meaning to gaze or stare intently.

ASPECT (ている):
{見|み}つめている indicates an ongoing action of gazing, often used to describe a sustained, intense look.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {目|め}を{見|み}つめる (gaze into someone's eyes)
- じっと{見|み}つめる (stare intently)
- {見|み}つめ{合|あ}う (gaze at each other)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}る: neutral looking
- {眺|なが}める: to gaze at scenery, more leisurely
- {睨|にら}む: to glare at (with hostility)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {見|み}つめ{直|なお}す: to reexamine, to take a fresh look at

[Register: Neutral]
